notes.title: Return to the Origins
notes.notes:
[p]Hello everyone, first of all I want to apologize for the long silence.[/p][p]These past months have been quite unusual, split between a very demanding work period and another side project that has been doing well.[/p][p]
This silence was due to my own indecision and a change of direction for Deity’s Domain, because the way the game was heading no longer satisfied me.
The game was moving toward a structure that was too story driven and not “free” enough compared to what I originally had in mind. Deity’s Domain started with the idea of being a complete sandbox, but the feeling when playing was not that of being a deity, more like a babysitter managing their city.
So I decided to start over. I know many of you may not like this, but since I am developing Deity’s in my free time and for personal enjoyment, I did not want to continue with something that would have been more of a burden than a passion. For sure, I would not have reached the kind of result I had envisioned from the very beginning.[/p][p]If you are wondering what I am aiming for with this new beginning and what will remain from what we have seen, I will try to give you a vision of the direction I would like to take.
I am aiming for a pure sandbox. To give the true powers of a deity, you need an entire world, a world that can be shaped from its very beginning, a world where you can act in total freedom: creating mountains, raising and lowering sea levels, or draining them down to the abyss. I want you to be the ones to create forests, resources, and life.
I want the player to see cities being born and growing, to be able to wipe out all forms of life and start again, or to nurture them and make them prosper, whether simply for the pleasure of seeing them destroyed or of watching what they created flourish.
So there will be less direct city management than before, but management more focused on the whole and on the balance of the world’s ecosystem.
The giant hand you are used to seeing in Deity’s will remain and move as it always has, but it will act on a round planet and oversee the entire domain, from the birth of the planet as a ball of rock to its later version full of water and life.
And you will be able to freely look at every corner of your domain, from space down to the cities and the life inhabiting them.
The setting will also not change: it will remain Norse and mythological.[/p][p][/p][p]I am also aware this will extend development time, even if much of the existing logic can be reused.[/p][p][/p][p]I will leave you with a couple of screenshots to show the potential of the system I have created so far:

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45051315/c7c048563abc6a6023c752f0fb55481a0fafe989.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45051315/bae1e421d904ec1a187e6748289964848c98b313.png"][/img][/p][p]Updates will not be constant and monthly as before, but I will return from time to time to keep you posted, and when the moment comes I will also update the Steam page.[/p][p]Thank you for your patience and for following me this far. If you have doubts or questions, feel free to write them in the comments, I will answer every question.[/p][p][/p][p] See you soon with future updates.[/p]

notes.title: A Few Updates for a Quiet June
notes.notes: [p]Hello, little deities![/p][p]It’s been an incredibly busy month. At work I moved to a new department, and most of my mental energy went into learning the ins and outs of game-AI (not the kind everyone’s talking about lately, but the AI in videogames). On top of that, my personal life filled up fast with trips and summer activities I really needed.[/p][p]Here’s what’s new:[/p][list][*][p][b]Feedback implementation:[/b] I’ve rolled out several changes based on your last round of feedback.[/p][/*][*][p][b]New features from testing:[/b] A handful of essential features surfaced during our most recent tests—but so far that’s only about 30% of what I hoped to accomplish. I’ll be dedicating this final week of June exclusively to squashing bugs.[/p][/*][/list][p]Most of these updates pave the way for a [b]“Divine Vision Mode,”[/b] letting you flip into an all-seeing view that shows every citizen’s faith level, current tasks, and more.[/p][p]I’ve decided to skip a formal June devlog, but don’t worry, updates will still drop in July and August. Testing will pick back up after the summer break so I can fully recharge and come back stronger.[/p][p]Be good, and I’ll see you in the next update! 😉[/p]

notes.title: Next Steps
notes.notes:
Hello, deities! (Heilà Phil)

I’d like to thank everyone who took part in testing the demo your feedback, bug reports, and gameplay input have been incredibly helpful. It’s always magical to see someone else playing what I’m creating, and that magic is thanks in large part to you.

You’ve uncovered a whole bunch of new bugs, so it’s back to work to fix them all. But thanks to some of you, we’ve also identified improvements that will make the game experience easier to use and understand.

There isn’t much to report for this month it was mostly focused on preparing the build and gathering feedback. In June, I’ll be tackling the bugs you found, expanding the tutorials to cover the less obvious areas of the game, and completing the secondary features.

After that, I’ll shift my attention to game balance, which was completely sidelined in this demo. The next round of tests will be specifically aimed at balancing and enhancing the sense of progression within the game.

That means the next tests likely won’t reopen until the second half of July. Participation will, of course, be open to everyone who’s been involved so far and to others who haven’t yet received an access key.

Thanks again to you all see you in the next devlog! ;)

notes.title: Closed playtests for the demo have started!
notes.notes:
Hey everyone! I've reopened playtesting for the Deity's Domain demo.
If you’d like to participate, just send an email to: marketing@unlikelygs.com

Please include the following three things in your email:

[olist]
[*] The hardware specs of the PC you’ll be testing on
[*] Your Discord nickname
[*] Whether you’re available to record your first gameplay session (no audio or voiceover) and share the video with me via Discord. This isn’t mandatory but is greatly appreciated, as it would really help me improve the game.
[/olist]

[b]If you’re selected for the test, I’ll send you a Steam key that grants access to this and all future tests.[/b]

[b]What will you be testing?[/b]
[list]
[*]The early game tutorials up to what will be the end of the demo, which is planned for release here on Steam later this year. The demo lasts about 30 minutes to 1 hour.
[/list]

[b]What’s the purpose of this playtest?[/b]
[list]
[*] The goal is to assess the overall stability of the game. I want to identify any major blocking bugs and see whether the tutorials are clear and easy to follow.
[/list]

[b]So is the demo almost ready?[/b]
[list]
[*] Not quite. The game isn’t balanced yet, especially when it comes to Food and Power mechanics. The current demo is missing many minor features, contains various minor to medium bugs, has very few sound effects and visual effects, and only about 25% of the planned miracles (both for the player and the enemies) are available. There’s just one side quest at the moment.
[/list]

[b]Will there be future opportunities for those who aren't selected?[/b]
[list]
[*] Yes. Everyone who sends an email will be added to a list and considered for future tests. I’ll also make announcements when new testing phases begin. And even if you're never selected, you’ll still be able to play the demo once it releases publicly (Q4 2025).
[/list]

[b]How long will the playtest be available?[/b]
[list]
[*] The game will be available to play until May 25th. After that, access will be closed. If too many major bugs show up, I may need to shut it down earlier.
[/list]

[b]Why is access granted via email, and what’s the gameplay video for?[/b]
[list]
[*] Steam’s built-in playtest system doesn’t allow for direct communication with testers. At this early stage, I need a more personal channel for bug reports and feedback.
[*] The video gives me a clearer understanding of the issues players encounter and helps me spot patterns and behaviors I didn’t anticipate.
[/list]

Thanks so much for your attention, little deities!

notes.title: Deity's Domain - Devlog 10 - UI rework, Road system polishing and bugfixing!
notes.notes:
Here we are again for our monthly update. April has flown by it was a month of many highs and lows, but nonetheless full of achievements for Deity’s.

Last month, I mentioned a few small changes I wanted to make to player progression within the game. I went ahead and implemented them, and the new Faith-resource mechanic has proven very effective.

This month, I applied another series of changes that I personally felt were essential in a game like this. From the very start of development, my goal was to create a game without a permanent on-screen UI. However, during development that principle wasn’t maintained mostly because quick solutions were needed to display essential information. So I took some time to revisit the UI and its usability in order to bring the game back in line with that original goal. I’m well on my way: most of the process is complete, though a few tweaks and decisions remain. I expect to finish these changes in May.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45051315/ddac32c3367001509b3203c5eb0e57dffbae3e33.png[/img]


Now that information is scattered around the Island, I’ve also added a “fast travel” system accessed via a radial menu. After discovering points of interest or building specific structures that you’ll need to visit often (for example, the warehouse), the menu will show dedicated inputs to move you quickly to those locations.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45051315/bd63cc0be743a93fd926c68cd99f72816eaaaa4c.png[/img]

Continuing the polishing work we began last month, I wrapped up the road-building system adding a much more elegant preview, implementing an actual construction cost, and fixing a large number of related bugs.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45051315/0fac5aba1be46c40a3520d3413e19658d09f1191.png[/img]

But the biggest challenge these past weeks has been the pathfinding. Almost every tester reported citizens getting stuck or endlessly falling. I investigated thoroughly and discovered that, after a variable amount of time in the shipping build, pathfinding nodes weren’t always updating correctly after buildings were constructed. Solving this turned out to be lengthy and complex, but it has eliminated most of the citizen-movement issues.

I plan to spend all of May refining the UI rework and polishing the critical points identified in previous tests, while continuing to push out fixes. I’ll likely limit testing in May to those who already have access, and if all goes well in the next devlog I’ll open testing to new users.

So please keep following the project and spread the word. See you soon, little deities!

notes.title: Deity's Domain - Devlog 9 - Citizens polishing, bug fixing and new tests!
notes.notes:
Here we are with our monthly update, how are you doing? I hope well!
March was almost entirely focused on polishing the citizens, especially in the first half of the month.

Several small details were added for example, citizens now have a proper animation for transporting resources, and the type of resource they’re carrying is visible.
A new “alert” state was also introduced: if a citizen takes damage or dies (not from old age), nearby citizens will flee in the opposite direction. This alert state can also be triggered by urgent actions, like fetching water from the well or reaching a fire site (yes, buildings can now catch fire!).

[previewyoutube=mKO1N_rQH9E;full][/previewyoutube]

I also worked on a rework of the audio manager, updated the game’s music, and gave the roads a visual overhaul.

[previewyoutube=HO5SU3BEUHY;full][/previewyoutube]

In the second half of the month, I started expanding testing and brought in new people and wow… I received a flood of bug reports.
I’ve been doing this job for nearly a decade, so I know how normal this is especially when you’re working solo. When you’re developing something of your own, you often go into “self-defense” mode: you test things in the safest way possible out of fear of breaking them, or you run tests just to confirm they behave the way you expect.
But players don’t play “safely.” And that’s exactly why I’m running these tests, and I’m genuinely happy with what the testers have pointed out.

They’ve also been super helpful in highlighting the weaknesses of the tutorial system its pacing, the storytelling, which led me to make a few design changes.
Nothing drastic or game changing, but small adjustments aimed at keeping your deity more actively involved in managing the world.

For example, previously, progressing through the game phases only required accumulating a certain amount of Glory, which is passively generated at the Temple. This mechanic won’t change but now you’ll need to actively spend Glory, deciding whether to offer it to a Positive or Negative target, along with other similar changes.

[previewyoutube=2vGov18k56w;full][/previewyoutube]

I also started adding a few puzzles and points of interest around the island. These will later be tied into the gameplay logic to trigger side quests and dialogues. However, in the demo they’ll be limited probably only two events will be available.

As the months go by, a possible release date for the demo is becoming more and more defined. It’s not set in stone yet, anything can happen, but the current planned release date on my schedule is October of this year.

Stay tuned! I’ll be needing testers closer to release. But for now, there’s still a lot to do to make the game more solid, and I need to focus on fixing all the bugs.

Thanks again for following along this far, see you in April with the next DevLog!

notes.title: Deity's Domain - Devlog 8
notes.notes:
Hello, little deities, and welcome to the 8th monthly update!

February was primarily focused on adding tutorials and the necessary features to help you get started on the island. 
There has been a major upgrade to the system that allows enemy deities to intervene on the island they can now unleash fires and famines upon your city and its citizens, and finally, you can perform sacrifices, whether of resources or... humans. 
However, for too long I’ve only been writing about it, now I’d like to give you a small, concrete preview of some of the features already available in the game:

[previewyoutube=5xE9NlrYSvI;full][/previewyoutube]

Obviously, this is still far from the final version of the demo. Many small features are still missing, and I have yet to connect several systems that are already implemented, such as the alignment system, etc.

There are also various visual bugs, and all visual effects are still missing from the cutscenes, but I still wanted to give back to all of you who have been following me for so many months.

There's still a lot of polish to do, but testing and the demo are getting closer and closer. And maybe in the coming months, I'll have another piece of news that might interest the most active among you.

Don't hesitate to share the video if you liked it!

As always, if you have any questions, curiosities, or suggestions, feel free to comment below.

See you soon, and keep following us, little deities!

notes.title: Deity's Domain - Devlog 7
notes.notes:
Hello, little deities, and welcome to the 7th monthly update.

After taking a short Christmas break, here we are again at our regular meeting. How's it going? I hope all is well.

The past few months have been very important for Deity's Domain, I have finally reached one of the major milestones. The foundations for all the features planned for the demo have finally been completed! I have started running initial tests by sharing a first build of the game with friends and colleagues in the industry.

The last major missing feature was the enemy deities and the Norne's Thread. The Norne's Thread is an item that the player will receive shortly after the game begins. This thread allows them to see the imminent future of the Island, with nodes appearing on it that we can examine. For example, a node might appear at the top of the thread, and by bringing our hand over it, we will notice that deity X will cast an Incendiary Miracle on a house in our City. We will be able to see which house will be targeted and act accordingly perhaps protecting it with a Barrier Miracle or conserving Power for another purpose and letting the house burn, leaving it to the citizens to deal with.

What is the purpose of this system and why did I want to include it? The competition between the Deities is a competition for Faith, each deity will strive to gain more followers and maintain them for as long as possible. Their faith is obtained in various ways, but the primary method is having a direct impact on their lives, whether positive or negative. Even setting a house on fire, as in the example above, will cause some citizens to convert to the deity that is currently having the most impact on their lives.

Additionally, a Deity should have the power to see things inaccessible to others. In ancient Norse mythology, destiny was traced by the Norne, and from this concept arose the idea of giving each deity access to the thread of their own island... their own Domain. However, the thread cannot show everything; there are Powers and Miracles that go beyond what the thread can reveal.

Another piece of good news concerns the AI: finally, the new system is completely integrated and stable. In the last days of January, I decided to add a new type of resource (Stone) and creating the AI behavior for collection and management was really a piece of cake it took just over an hour.

As mentioned at the beginning, I started having friends and colleagues test the build, mainly to understand the feel of the basic systems, and I am really satisfied with the initial results. These tests have led to changes in resource management and game economy, and have made me realize that there is still much to do from a user experience standpoint.

Now that the game's skeleton is ready, I will start focusing much more on user experience, polish, and functionality integration. There are still many tutorials, essential tooltips, 90% of the Miracles, visual and audio effects missing—in short, the descent begins, but it's still a long descent.

However, don't despair. Before releasing the demo, I will need testers and feedback. So for the more curious, there might be early access slots. I cannot be certain of the timeframe, but I hope to start testing around mid-year and release the demo in Q4 2025.

The tests will be conducted here on Steam for limited periods of time. I will ask participants (if available and with your consent) to share gameplay videos and fill out a feedback form, which will be invaluable for improving the game.

As always, if you have any questions, curiosities, or suggestions, feel free to comment below ːsteammockingː

See you soon, and keep following us, little deities!

notes.title: Deity's Domain - Devlog 6
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45051315/c6ff7f1dcad72615b998741f9a3168bdfcf78cab.png[/img]

This image captures much of this month. It may seem like little, but I assure you it was not.

But let’s take it step by step:

This month began with the implementation of new cinematics and tutorials. Everything was going smoothly until I reached the cinematic where the first citizens arrive on the island. I was very satisfied. Along the way, I also cleaned up and refined many existing systems and created various useful ways for the game to communicate important information to the player.  
However, as I started working on the first tutorials for managing citizens and the city, an annoyance grew within me hour by hour. Damn it, I had programmed every behavior of these citizens. I knew exactly when and how they would do everything. But that was not what I wanted from the start. I wanted something unpredictable, even for me as the developer, something that would prevent citizens from simply doing A, B, and then C because that is how it was programmed.

So midway through the month, I decided to scrap what I had done with my Context System and move to a more robust and well-known approach. This brings an endless array of possibilities. I decided to switch to AI based on GOAP, Goal-Oriented Action Planning. On top of that, I also focused on creating a specific Octree for this project. Let me explain.

Previously, if we wanted a citizen to build a structure, the building to be constructed would be placed on the map. It would then notify the Context Manager that X citizens were needed for the construction. These citizens would be assigned to a Context and given a Task, which would generate jobs defined by the Task. However, if at some point in development we decided that wood for building houses could also be gathered from debris of destroyed houses, this information and behavior would have to be explicitly added.  
With GOAP, this is no longer necessary. Now, when a building is added, it searches the Octree for a suitable citizen and assigns them a Goal. For example, the Goal might specify that the building needs 100 wood to be completed. The GOAP solver will then look for the nearest Action to the citizen that, in its definition, indicates it provides wood. The citizen will execute that Action because it satisfies the Goal assigned to them. This happens without directly scripting what the citizen should do. Only the Actions need to be scripted, but in an atomic and independent way, detached from the final Goal.

Apologies if I got too technical, but I hope the idea is clear.

Now I need to convert all previous logic to this new system. I trust this will not take too long and then I can return to the main development of the story, tutorials, and quests.

But that is not all that happened this month.  
You have probably noticed the rework of the game’s art here on Steam. Do you like it? Let me know your thoughts in the comments.  
The logo is temporary. I hope to rework it in the coming months, but it will stay as it is for now.

Additionally, there has been a massive improvement to the day-night cycle. Daylight duration has been significantly increased, now covering 75% of a full day. The transition between day and night is much smoother and the nighttime lighting has been adjusted to improve visibility and enhance the overall atmosphere.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45051315/fe2d38f69a8eb29a9dfe7aa11957ebcb78733b0f.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45051315/6c825f85eed51653d4291b0b0a4de419ccc6a472.png[/img]

To conclude, the project is progressing and I am increasingly happy with how it is shaping up. I cannot wait to reach the demo milestone to hear your thoughts and then get to work on making it even better. As I mentioned earlier, I am forging ahead with the implementation of tutorials, quests, and the journey from arriving on the island to just before unlocking our little Pet.

Keep following the project and if you have any doubts, questions, or even just want to chat about it, do not hesitate to comment or write in the dedicated Steam community.  
Thank you again and remember to always be good little deities!

notes.title: Deity's Domain - Devlog 5
notes.notes:
Hello, little deities, and welcome to the 5th monthly update.
This month has been intense in many ways, and though I've had less time than usual to continue development, I still managed to make some significant progress.

Last time, I talked about the updates to the faith system and the new rune-drawing system on the ground. Both seem to be working well, and this month I've continued developing these systems by integrating a UI that makes it easier to visualize the Power of Faith and Glory that the player possesses.

Power (the yellow sphere in the center) is the resource that allows you to cast miracles and runes. Faith is represented by the blue percentage bar, showing the contribution of faith from your citizens. The arrows, which can turn purple, indicate the trend of faith. Glory is another percentage value that tracks progress toward the next divine level.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45051315/b3b0b6a921366b513a50468aec4395c72b61c451.png[/img]

I’m happy with the result—I don’t want to clutter the game with too much UI, so having all this information in a single spot seemed like the best idea.

In addition to this, I improved the weather system. You can now perform miracles to change various weather types. Plants react to the wind, and the snow system has been completely reworked. I’ve added clouds that grow, shrink, and change color, and added post-process effects to make the visuals darker during storms. I’ll improve it further in the future with sound effects and additional visual elements like thunder and lightning, etc.

(Sorry for the low quality, it is extracted from a larger video shot while using the engine, so it has a lower quality recording)
[previewyoutube=t2a8lGj8IH4;full][/previewyoutube]

The rune and sign system has also been improved. Now, after drawing them, you need to confirm by drawing a circle around the rune to validate it or an X to cancel it.

I’ve made progress on quests and tutorials as well, and I’ve created a first draft of the cinematic system. So far, I haven't advanced much with the tutorials because I’ve been focusing on polishing what’s already in place. I hope to continue this work in November.

[previewyoutube=It9rrkSohpM;full][/previewyoutube]

If I were to describe the current state of the game with a metaphor, I’d compare it to writing a book. It’s as if I have a lot of material ready, at least enough for a demo, but I still need to gather all the scattered pages and write the story in an organized way.

There are still two major features missing (which I’ll tell you about in the future), and there’s plenty of polishing and tutorials/quests to prepare. So, stay tuned and make sure you don’t miss any news.

And we'll finish with an update on the citizen rework: our 3D modeler Victor has completed the modeling of the new citizens. We just need to add more detailed and colorful textures, but they've already been integrated into the game.

See you soon, and keep following us, little deities!

PS: You may have noticed I’ve updated all the screenshots on the Steam page. I’ll gradually update the entire page as development progresses. I’d love to hear what you think. Thanks again, everyone!

notes.title: Deity's Domain - Devlog 4
notes.notes:
Hello, little deities! Welcome back to our monthly update, and thank you for your continued interest in the project.

September has been quite a unique month. I was on vacation for almost two weeks, yet I managed to maintain a good level of productivity and keep progressing toward my goals. The two weeks of rest were truly "miraculous," allowing me to return fully refreshed. So, without further ado, let's dive into the updates.

This month has also been filled with reworks and improvements. Unfortunately, most of these changes aren't directly visible, but don’t worry—there’s still plenty to showcase.

In recent days, I've implemented the "Social System," a procedural system that assigns a "personality" to each family. This system activates whenever members of different families interact, and their compatibility affects the relationship between them. These values will then be used to enhance citizen interactions, allowing them to engage in activities influenced by their relationships. Integrating this system revealed a bunch of bugs; it took some time, but now it seems to be working great! 😉

Another significant rework involved the Faith System, aiming to simplify the information presented to the player. We shifted from a system based on the faith of each individual citizen to a single value representing all followers. Along with this, I implemented much of the deity's "power" system, which governs the gathering and consumption of the resource that allows the deity to cast spells and enchantments. In addition, I revamped the structure of the Temple to reflect the current Faith value (through the size of the tallest blue flame, which shrinks or grows based on Faith) and the current level of Glory (or Fear/Love, depending on your alignment) through the smaller braziers.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45051315/b1ca26099655f250ae882a5c347be9443ef720fe.jpg[/img]

Another major feature that landed in Deity's Domain this month is the ability to draw runes on the ground. Creating a system that accurately recognizes what the deity has drawn was no easy task, but it seems like we’ve achieved the goal. In short, I collect the drawn points, use the camera's direction to define a canvas for the drawing, and then convert this into a texture. This texture is divided into 16 sections and compared against a database. Based on the matching value of each section, a final similarity score is generated, and it's working well—even for runes that are quite similar.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45051315/1561736d3de785a167f657c9e185544b127fcab2.gif[/img]

(And the keenest among you may have also noticed the floating message that appears after the rune is activated; it’s part of a small implementation aimed at enhancing the user experience in various situations)

Finally, let’s wrap up with an update on the new citizens. We're transitioning from concept art to 3D models and running the first rigging tests to ensure a smooth transition from the old to the new models. We can’t wait to see them textured and wandering around in the world of Deity's Domain.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45051315/0f192f138f4972f2aaeaafd34787e680f56c2ac0.png[/img]

The project is moving quickly. Unfortunately (or fortunately), I keep finding new features to add to the game. Or, as in the case of the Faith System, I realize that already-implemented systems require major adjustments to better integrate with the game's structure, which might slightly extend the development time. However, the current goal remains the Demo, and month after month, I feel we’re getting closer to reaching the quality needed for this milestone.

Don't stop following us to stay updated; big things are on the horizon!

As always, if you have any questions, curiosities, or suggestions, feel free to comment below ːsteamhappyː 

See you soon, and keep following us, little deities!

notes.title: Deity's Domain - Devlog 3
notes.notes:
Hello little deities, welcome back to our monthly update! As always, I've been eagerly awaiting this moment to share the latest developments with you.

This month has been incredibly productive. I took advantage of a week off from my main job to make significant progress on Deity's Domain, so let's go dive into the news:

I am happy to announce that the next milestone for the project will be the [b]Demo[/b], which will cover the beginning of the game up to the end of the first phase (there will be three phases in total), with an estimated duration of about 2 hours. The first phase is much shorter than the subsequent ones.

Please note that this first version of the demo will stop just before the acquisition of the creature, which will be included in a second version of the demo. It's a very delicate feature, and I want to take my time to get it right.

As I mentioned at the end of the last devlog, this month I focused primarily on implementing a quest and tutorial system. I'm quite satisfied with the result; I now have a very flexible system that will allow me to outline all the events from here to the demo and later for the entire game.
Most of the tutorials have already been implemented, but they are still placeholders. They need polishing and the addition of events and artistic effects.

Significant progress has also been made with the sound design and visual effects, but it’s still too early to show anything in that regard. These are mainly targeted interventions aimed at consolidating the systems for future polishing.

Another big update is the new map [b][Work in progress][/b]! The one you’ve seen so far was temporary and had a small advantage that was convenient during the early stages of prototyping and development... it was flat. However, I've always wanted to move to a larger island, especially one structured on various slopes, but this brings many complications from an implementation standpoint. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45051315/404edf7cd9eaeed583048b80966aae16ffd21568.jpg[/img]

So this month, I focused on identifying the technical limitations that were holding me back and addressed them. In particular, it was impossible with the old system of fields to play on sloped terrain, so I completely rewrote the system, moving from a fixed grid system to a four-point system that creates a more flexible grid, effectively changing the underlying terrain type.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45051315/02c791045d1b34f7088fbc8e32bd4cd4709f5297.gif[/img]

I’m very pleased with this result, and I’m sure this system will be useful for many other objectives 😉

Some modifications were also necessary for the structures, but nothing too interesting.

Together with the 3D modeler, we’re starting to work on reworking the citizens to increase the variety and quality of your future citizens and (hopefully) followers, here's a little preview of the concept:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45051315/77d7157af9d6237d1dd25524518d7d91ebdf660e.png[/img]

There are two more updates. One of them is visible, and the sharp-eyed among you may have noticed—there has been a UI rework. This was a step I wanted to take some time ago when we moved to the Norse setting, but I took some extra time to decide on the style to use. I hope you like this new direction. Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments if you’d like 😉

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45051315/df9d2043ca149d8cc6b729a78b682d234a351ded.jpg[/img]

Lastly, over the past few weeks, I’ve also been working on a system similar to Unreal’s GAS (Gameplay Ability System). If any of you developers have worked with Unreal, you’ll know how powerful this system is. I use it every day in my main job, and I have to say it’s fantastic. However, since Unity doesn't officially have anything like it, and the GAS systems available online didn’t quite meet my needs, I’ve been creating my own, with great results. This should speed up development in the long run, though it has required a very thorough restructuring at present. But I’m almost done, and the positive effects of this new development system are already noticeable.

So, looking back on this month, I can say I'm satisfied. The groundwork has been laid for everything needed for the upcoming demo. Please note that it will still take some time; the hope is to have a first public and playable demo available by Q1 2025. However, I can't provide a definitive date just yet, so stay tuned for future updates. I'm already looking forward to our next regular update.

See you soon, and keep following us, little deities!

notes.title: Deity's Domain - Devlog 2
notes.notes:
Hello little deities, here we are again for our monthly update. I'm really happy to see that more and more of you are joining us.

The rework of the citizens' AI that I started last month has finally been completed, and I am really satisfied with the results. If you've read the previous major news before this dev log, you know that the setting of Deity's Domain is shifting from a Roman to a Norse theme. This change within the game is almost complete. However, it will take some time to recreate the materials to apply this change to the Steam page. I hope to complete everything by mid-August.

The transition has been smooth and problem-free for all structures, resources, and the map. However, the rework of the citizens required a bit more effort. Working with character models, skeletons for animations, and so on, always turns into a huge mess, but in the end, we came out victorious. Here are some examples of the issues we encountered ːsteamsaltyː:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45051315/4cd3c70858087e163f4a868349b22fc5d8c44018.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45051315/b0d11c6cfb3d41968c394f71c688f27e651e5f60.png[/img]

Now, let's move on to the substantial matters. I would like to show you the restyling of all the structures implemented in the game so far:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45051315/f4d099a3536a3d5bd59809d38ab93aba33b1cc74.jpg[/img]

For the creation of each element, I sought references closely related to Norse culture, except for the temple, for which I took the liberty of using a reference closer to a druidic temple than a Nordic structure. Showing the first images of the change, I was often asked if I intended to add snow to the game. Deity's Domain has a food mechanic based on 3-day cycles (this value is provisional and subject to future changes), so I thought snow would be a great visual element to help mark these cycles. Thus, I implemented a weather system to handle this: (Sorry for the low GIF quality, but I had to compress it a lot to fit it here ːsteamsadː)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45051315/6911b0d5a044d836338edade94eba43d906a57cf.gif[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45051315/0c4b9320f913d320c9891824052a7a17637cf8cb.gif[/img]

As you can see from these images, I took the time to implement another aesthetic aspect very useful for adding a bit more mood. Now, each structure has torches that will light up and extinguish based on the time of day. 

Additionally, the 3D model of the scale to be used in the warehouse has arrived. In Deity's Domain, you can ration the food to be assigned to the citizens, with rations ranging from six categories (no ration, one-quarter, half, normal, double, and triple). The whole process happens without the use of an interface. Simply clicking on one or the other plate of the scale will adjust the amount of food consumed by each citizen. The mechanic is already present and functional in the game. I will add the aesthetic and animation aspects soon:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45051315/9af5266ca13220ab70850173f6fec196b0d8f922.png[/img]

Besides this, I have started working on the system for inspecting and interacting with citizens, which is the mechanic that will allow you to read citizens' desires, delve into their characteristics, punish them, bless them, and so on. There's still much to do here and not much to show yet. I have created a definitive roadmap for the Demo and the first part of the gameplay, which ranges from entering the game with the respective tutorials to obtaining the creature. I will release details and publish it when I am sure of the realization times.

In the coming months and until the first playable version, I will focus on implementing this roadmap. A good starting point will be the creation of a solid tutorial system to be used throughout all game phases. Thank you again for following me this far. Your interest means a lot to me, and I can't wait to show you more. Leave a like, and if you have any doubts or questions, don't hesitate to let me know in the comments below.

Keep following the game for more news ːsteamhappyː

notes.title: A big change
notes.notes:
Hello everyone, I’m here to make a very important announcement regarding the game. After thorough reflection, which actually began months ago, even before the game's announcement, I have decided to change the game's setting from Roman to Norse.

When the idea for Deity's Domain was born, I thought long and hard about which setting to choose, and from the start, it came down to two options: Roman or Norse. After a series of research and studies, I decided to proceed with the Roman setting. However, as development progressed, I realized that the setting and artistic style were drifting too far from what I wanted for the project. I needed a setting that was less "clean" and more "rugged," a mythology rich in mysteries, fantastic creatures, and one that allows for much more imagination. So, over the months, I started experimenting with small changes in mood, lighting, and models to see if this change made sense, and in the end, I understood that this was what I wanted for Deity's Domain.

However, I want to make it clear that this change only affects the game's setting and aesthetics. The design remains completely unchanged, with only some minor adjustments to the narrative, but even here, nothing too drastic from what I initially planned.

I know some of you were very attached to the Roman setting, which I also love dearly, but I believe this new aesthetic can offer much more to Deity's Domain and to what I have wanted to convey from the beginning, we are still at the beginning of the project. I believe that if this had to be done, this was the only suitable moment.

Thank you all very much for your attention and support. I'll leave you with a couple of behind-the-scenes screenshots of this change.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45051315/14c394ed9eb50ea0a9586c962faf780ad98e7a85.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45051315/1a59f2f6bde5d6ad4947314db976d263ae3e6e44.jpg[/img]

PS: The page will be updated as soon as all the material is ready and the transition to the new setting is complete.

For any doubts or questions, don't hesitate to comment here. I will read and respond to everything ːsteamhappyː

notes.title: Deity's Domain - Devlog I
notes.notes:
Here we are at the first dev log of Deity's Domain. First of all, I want to thank all of you for the support you've shown so far. There's nothing more rewarding than seeing people's reactions to the project we're working so hard on. Thanks to everyone who shared this page with their friends; it’s a great support.

A large part of this month was spent reorganizing the roadmap and setting clearer goals for the future of the project. It’s still too early to set precise dates, but it’s good to have soft dates as targets. Additionally, preparing material to showcase the game has taken up a significant portion of the available time.

I would have liked to spend more time balancing the existing mechanics, especially the population growth and faith mechanics, which, though implemented for some time, require an initial balance iteration. However, as a good programmer, I got lost in refactoring and consolidating the AI system and citizen management. I won’t go into too much detail to avoid boring you, but overall, I streamlined unnecessarily complicated logic and added another layer to the existing system to have better control over what’s happening in our Capital. Now I expect fewer bugs and glitches in our Citizens' routines. As you know, unlike other games, here the player can interact with every citizen at any time, directly or indirectly, adding many variables and complications that must be considered. Therefore, having a solid and scalable system at the base is even more critical, even if it means pausing the implementation of new features for a long period. This task will likely continue into part of July as well.

Between reworks, I found time to advance some utility tools within the project. Specifically, I implemented a system that will allow interaction with game objects without having to grab them directly, but instead "click" them like a button in a graphical interface. I hope to show you something about this soon; a practical demonstration will make it easier to understand the utility of this interaction tool within the world of Deity's Domain.

Additionally, the Engine (Unity) was updated from version 2023 to the new [url=https://unity.com/blog/engine-platform/unity-6-preview-release]Unity 6[/url], resulting in a decent reduction of CPU load and some minor improvements in lighting.

As I’ve mentioned in various points, I work on the project in my free time and during my commute. I spend about 3 hours traveling to and from work, and in nearly 2 of those hours, I work on the game using a laptop. While it’s a high-performance laptop, as the project grew larger, it started to become limiting. So at the beginning of the month, I built a new desktop PC to speed up the work when I’m at home, which has been a great help, significantly speeding up the debugging processes.

Now I'll stop with this boring stuff and move on to show you what has been produced for the game this month. Specifically, the modeling of some of the future structures in Deity's Domain has progressed:

[b]Arena:[/b] I want to clarify that we are not sure if this feature will be included in the final game, but we want to explore whether it makes sense to include an Arena in our Capital, which will allow our citizens to be entertained with fighting and blood shows.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45051315/7ca968b6acc5bb7897b4e7565dd0862e59008be8.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45051315/57fadb75a58eacae997c642fee8065e32cce8a6e.png[/img]

[b]Port (Work in Progress):[/b] The port will be a fundamental structure, unlocked in an advanced stage of the game, allowing interactions between populations across archipelagos. However, there’s still much work to be done before we can see it in the game.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45051315/577fa08b6d7cf7b8acc7dd3d4f9b0c718e765acf.png[/img]

To close, I’d like to show you some animations of the Creature we are working on. So far, during the prototyping phase, we’ve been using generic "Humanoid" animations, and it was time to create custom animations for the Creature. It’s still too early to show anything, but I admit I can’t wait to share news about it with you!

[b]Walk:[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45051315/544a07b24aaf0a82a7e5fe33bbd229427ea6b187.gif[/img]
[b]Run:[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45051315/bbbcfc28824f087d5ad6e94fcef550393a6c2a1d.gif[/img]
[b]Pickup:[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45051315/2d91f78e972cb87a33d565a0bf464f8626bd41dc.gif[/img]
[b]Drop[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45051315/d35abb493ff7c2e6ded958d587a87e13ce7363e1.gif[/img]

[b]For the next blog[/b], I hope to have completed the rework of the Citizens' AI, so I can get back to adding the features I’ve planned. Over the next two months, I hope to add some progression features for the City and the Deity. After that, I plan to return to working on the Creature to start giving it an AI worthy of the name.

That’s all for this devlog. I’m really excited to have this space to let you know how things are progressing. I can’t wait to read your comments; if you have any questions, feel free to ask below or let me know what you think.

Thanks again for your attention, and see you very soon! ;)

notes.title: F.A.Q
notes.notes:
[b]Is Deity's Domain a remake of Black & White?[/b]
No, Deity's Domain is not intended to be Black & White 3 nor a remake of the series. The game is heavily inspired by it but takes a completely different path and setting.

[b]What will be the main similarities with Lionhead Studio's masterpiece?[/b]
Deity's Domain adopts almost entirely the movement and interaction system with the world, the deity alignment system, and has a creature management system.

[b]How many people are developing the game? What is Unlikely Studio?[/b]
Currently, the game is developed by a single person, me ;) However, I am constantly supported by other collaborators who handle specific parts of the game for me, such as creating 3D models and animations.
I have been making video games for several years, having released games of all sizes and for almost every device, so this is not my first game. If there's something to be done, I always know what is within the realm of possibilities.

[b]In Deity's Domain, will it be possible to create, command, and have military units fight?[/b]
The initial game design included these mechanics, however, during evaluation, we decided to remove (or postpone) them because they would require a significant amount of resources. We preferred to consider adding them in the future rather than integrating them at launch without the level of quality we desired.

[b]Is the game set in a single era and civilization?[/b]
Exactly, Deity's Domain is set in ancient Norse and and draws inspiration from that mythology.

[b]Will there be various "Lands" like in Black & White?[/b]
Deity's Domain is set in an archipelago. Your capital will be on one of these islands, and it will remain yours until the end of the game. I didn't like the idea of constantly moving the player from one island to another, always starting over. I have always preferred a linear progression of the city, the people, and the deity.

[b]Will there be ways to interact with the other islands and other deities?[/b]
Yes, during the game, you will increase your influence enough to interact with the other islands. You won't be able to observe and interact with them in as much detail as your own island, but you will be able to cast miracles, send units to convert enemy populations, saboteurs, etc.

[b]Will there be a story or will it be a pure Sandbox?[/b]
Yes, there will be a story. The ultimate goal of your deity will be to grow enough to be admitted among the major deities after a cataclysm has left a spot open. However, we would like to add a fully Sandbox mode in the future, but we believe some extra mechanics are necessary to make a mode entirely focused on freedom enjoyable.
